problem_markdown: A function $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ has $f(m+n)-f(m)-f(n)\in\{0,1\}$, $f(2)=0$, $f(3)>0$, and $f(9999)=3333$. Determine $f(1982)$.
solutions_markdown:
The condition at $1+1$ gives $f(1)=0$, and then $f(3)=1$. Repeated superadditivity gives $f(3k)\ge k$. If this were strict for any $k\le3333$, adding $3333-k$ further threes would contradict $f(9999)=3333$. Thus $f(3k)=k$ throughout that range.

Now $1982=1980+2$ gives $f(1982)\ge f(1980)=660$. On the other hand,
$$3f(1982)\le f(5946)=1982,$$
so the integer $f(1982)\le660$. Hence it equals $660$. The data are consistent, for example with $f(n)=\lfloor n/3\rfloor$.
